holidays.name: National Potato Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble spud in all its glory, from crispy fries and fluffy mashed potatoes to hash browns, chips, and loaded bakes. Any potato dish counts, and the more butter, the better.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance with no single documented founder. It has grown through food-lover and restaurant culture, and potatoes have been cultivated in the Andes for thousands of years.
holidays.funFact: The potato is one of the world's most important food crops, ranking fourth globally behind rice, wheat, and corn.

holidays.name: World Photography Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the art and craft of photography. Everyone is invited to grab a camera or phone, capture a single frame worth remembering, and share it with someone else.
holidays.origin: The date marks August 19, 1839, when the French government announced the daguerreotype process and gave it as a free gift to the world. That made photography widely accessible.
holidays.funFact: People now take well over a trillion photos every year, far more than were taken in the first 150 years of photography.

holidays.name: National Aviation Day
holidays.description: A day for looking skyward and celebrating pilots, engineers, and the history of flight. Make paper airplanes, visit an airfield, or hold a distance contest with friends.
holidays.origin: President Franklin D. Roosevelt established it by proclamation in 1939 to mark the birthday of Orville Wright, who was born on August 19, 1871.
holidays.funFact: Orville Wright piloted the first powered, controlled airplane flight in 1903. It lasted just 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, which is shorter than the wingspan of many modern jumbo jets.
